purpose: Record the exact chain from a published research result to a project decision, implementation, learner action, retained evidence and claim boundary.

source.title: Cyber-SHIP: Developing Next Generation Maritime Cyber Research Capabilities
source.authors: Kimberly Tam, Kevin Forshaw and Kevin Jones

translations.finding_used: Maritime cyber research needs configurable, connected ship systems and an explicit choice among simulation, emulation and live equipment; system-of-systems behavior matters.
translations.engineering_decision: Model the Cargo, power-management and propulsion-auxiliary domains as a coupled vessel system, and label the fidelity of every major layer instead of calling the software stack a ship digital twin.
translations.learner_action: Run the generator-trip scenario and trace the event from the PMS state through vessel power availability to Cargo or machinery consequence, while identifying which parts are simulated, emulated or real software.
translations.falsification_condition: The translation fails if the domains remain independent, if only a dashboard value changes, or if the retained timeline cannot establish a cross-system consequence after the generator trip.
excluded_claims: The project is not a physical twin of a vessel.
Software emulation is not claimed to have Cyber-SHIP's live-equipment realism.

source.title: The Cyber-MAR Project: First Results and Perspectives on the Use of Hybrid Cyber Ranges for Port Risk Assessment

translations.finding_used: Cyber-MAR builds scenarios by examining incidents, operational assets, functions and dependencies; its port example makes electrical supply a scenario driver because other operations depend on it.
translations.engineering_decision: Start the integrated vessel scenario with an operational dependency rather than a random cyberattack: the PMS supplies Cargo pump power and propulsion auxiliary power through the Vessel Coordinator.
translations.learner_action: Before assigning an attack label, test whether a reported Cargo or machinery failure is the downstream result of a power-system event.
translations.falsification_condition: The translation fails if loss of the teaching bus cannot change dependent power availability, or if event order cannot distinguish the initiating power event from its downstream effect.
excluded_claims: The project does not reproduce a port topology.
The project does not implement Cyber-MAR's risk or econometric layers.
The project does not claim equivalence to a hybrid range with physical assets.

source.title: MaCySTe: A virtual testbed for maritime cybersecurity
source.authors: Giacomo Longo, Alessandro Orlich, Stefano Musante, Alessio Merlo and Enrico Russo

translations.finding_used: MaCySTe demonstrates a modular virtual maritime testbed with ship-network components, scenarios, software PLCs, a Modbus bridge, attack tooling and monitoring add-ons.
translations.engineering_decision: Use replaceable open-source services with real protocol traffic, but add explicit LNG Cargo, PMS and propulsion process dynamics plus evidence contracts instead of copying a navigation-focused topology.
translations.learner_action: Follow one value across the process model, I/O mapping, Modbus response, PLC variable and network analysis rather than treating the testbed as a collection of containers.
translations.falsification_condition: The translation fails if the components cannot exchange the declared protocol data or if an experiment produces no independently inspectable process and network artifacts.
excluded_claims: The project is not a fork or reproduction of MaCySTe.
The project does not claim MaCySTe's navigation, RADAR or NMEA coverage.
Containerization alone is not treated as a research contribution.

source.title: Development of Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulation Test Bed to Verify and Validate Power Management System for LNG Carriers

translations.finding_used: The LNG-carrier PMS HIL study evaluates load sharing, load-dependent generator start, blackout prevention and preferential load behavior through scenario-based tests.
translations.engineering_decision: Make those PMS functions observable teaching behaviors: equalized generator loading, reserve-based second-generator start, an explicit blackout state and staged Cargo/hotel load shedding.
translations.learner_action: Establish the bus, apply demand, trip a generator and explain the order of breaker loss, frequency excursion, load shedding and downstream vessel effect.
translations.falsification_condition: The translation fails if the trip does not produce the declared causal sequence or if the evaluator passes without observing the intervention, breaker loss, excursion and vessel consequence.
excluded_claims: This is software-in-the-loop, not the paper's hardware-in-the-loop apparatus.
Generator ratings and thresholds are teaching assumptions, not values taken from the paper.
The project does not claim to replace factory acceptance testing.

source.title: Assessment of Cyber-Physical Intrusion Detection and Classification for Industrial Control Systems
source.authors: Nils Mueller, Charalampos Ziras and Kai Heussen

translations.finding_used: On the paper's dataset, combining physical-process and network features improved classification over a network-only counterpart and helped analyze attacks and faults together.
translations.engineering_decision: Require three separate explanations—network-only, process-only and cross-layer—and prohibit any superiority claim until repeated project runs support it.
translations.learner_action: Investigate the same event three times using network evidence alone, process evidence alone and both together; score event order, supported claims and unresolved uncertainty.
translations.falsification_condition: The project's prospective benefit is not supported if the cross-layer condition does not improve the predeclared reconstruction measures over the network-only condition across repeated runs.
excluded_claims: The paper's performance result is not transferred to this project.
No machine-learning detector from the paper is implemented here.
The project currently makes no evidence-backed claim that cross-layer analysis outperforms network-only analysis.

source.title: State-Aware Anomaly Detection for Industrial Control Systems
source.authors: Hamid Reza Ghaeini, Daniele Antonioli, Ferdinand Brasser, Ahmad-Reza Sadeghi and Nils Ole Tippenhauer

translations.finding_used: The paper shows why anomaly detection can use expected physical-process behavior and state-dependent residuals instead of relying only on traffic or a single fixed sensor value.
translations.engineering_decision: Add an independent Cargo mass-balance check that compares measured flow with flow inferred from tank-level change, and retain the residual as evidence separate from the Modbus capture.
translations.learner_action: Inject a deterministic flow-sensor bias, calculate tank-derived flow and decide whether command, equipment feedback and physical consequence still agree.
translations.falsification_condition: The implementation is not useful for this scenario if a declared sensor bias does not create a repeatable residual, or if healthy runs cross the declared threshold without an explained cause.
excluded_claims: The analyzer is not the paper's state-aware CUSUM detector.
It uses no trained model or 120 GB historical dataset.
Its fixed teaching threshold has not yet been validated as an operational alarm limit.
